title: AI Human Review and Approval Workflow Design

questions.question: Why is 'human in the loop' not enough by itself?
options: Because humans should never be asked to review AI output in an accountable workflow
Because review roles, approval gates, quality criteria, and appeal paths must be explicit
Because approval always happens automatically once the AI output passes a filter
Because quality criteria stop mattering as soon as a named reviewer is assigned
questions.explanation: Saying a human will review it stays a vague reassurance until the review role and authority, the approval gate, the quality criteria, and the appeal path are explicit — it is not an argument against human review, automatic approval, or dropping quality criteria.

questions.question: An AI workflow drafts HR decisions and a manager is expected to check them, but nobody has defined at which point in the process that check has to happen before the output goes out. Which of the lesson's four signals does this match most directly?
options: Decision authority — it is unclear who is actually allowed to make the final call here
Quality uncertainty — nobody knows how reliable the AI's drafted output really is
User impact — the output affects people whose interests the workflow must protect
Approval gap — no defined decision point exists where the output must be approved
questions.explanation: No defined point in the process where output must be approved is the lesson's approval-gap signal, closed with an approval gate — distinct from decision authority (who may decide), quality uncertainty (how reliable the output is), or user impact.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A final legal opinion on whether the AI workflow may be used in this process
A ranked human-review workflow plan with a control for each scenario
A deployed approval system wired into the team's production workflow
A model training job that learns from past reviewer approvals and rejections
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks scenarios and recommends review and approval controls — review role, approval gate, quality checklist, appeal path — it does not issue a legal opinion, deploy an approval system, or train a model.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: Hiding quality uncertainty from reviewers so approvals move through faster
Appeal path — a route for affected people to challenge an AI-supported decision
Skipping the named reviewer because the AI output looked convincing enough
Removing the approval gate so high-impact output reaches users without delay
questions.explanation: The lesson's controls are review role, approval gate, quality checklist, and appeal path — an appeal path lets affected people challenge a decision, unlike hiding uncertainty, skipping the reviewer, or removing the gate.

questions.question: When is a mandatory approval gate appropriate?
options: Only when the AI output is trivial and has no effect on any downstream decision
Only when no user or customer is affected by the outcome of the workflow at all
When impact and uncertainty are high and decision authority or user impact is involved
Never — informal peer review by a colleague always covers accountable approval
questions.explanation: Approval gates should be tied to impact and uncertainty, so high impact combined with decision authority or user impact is exactly the case — unlike trivial output, no affected users, or relying on informal peer review.

questions.question: What should a human review workflow define?
options: Only the prompt used to generate the AI output being reviewed in the workflow
Only the output format the AI must return so reviewers can read it quickly
No escalation path, since uncertain cases can be decided by the first reviewer
Review role, approval gate, quality checklist, and appeal path for the output
questions.explanation: A human review workflow defines the review role, the approval gate, the quality checklist, and the appeal path — not just the prompt, the output format, or a design with no escalation route for uncertain cases.
